items.title: IIFCL IPO: Govt to part sale stake, company to issue fresh shares
items.rss_summary: The government is looking to part sale its equity shareholding in IIFCL along with a fresh issue of shares by the company in the initial public offering (IPO), which is likely by the end of the current fiscal year, an official said. The Cabinet had earlier this year approved the IPO and listing of India Infrastructure Finance Company Ltd (IIFCL), and the work is on to file a draft paper with market regulator Sebi for approval. Without disclosing the quantum of stake dilution, the official said that while the government will reduce its stake by an offer for sale, IFCL will issue fresh shares to raise capital in the IPO. Set up in 2006, IIFCL is a wholly-owned government company providing long-term finances to viable infrastructure projects and is registered as a non-deposit taking non-banking finance company with the RBI. items.title: Vedanta seeks premium over imported LNG prices for Rajasthan gas sale
items.rss_summary: Vedanta Oil and Gas Ltd is seeking a premium over imported LNG prices for 1.80 million standard cubic metres per day (mmscmd) of natural gas from its Rajasthan block, putting the volume up for sale through an electronic auction. The three-month supply contract, running from January 1 to April 1, 2027, will be auctioned on December 14, according to a request for proposal dated November 20 and a draft gas sales agreement. Bidders have been asked to quote a premium they are willing to pay over the monthly average of Platts West India spot liquefied natural gas (LNG) prices, with the highest bids receiving priority in the allocation of available volumes. The starting premium is zero, with bids required to increase in increments of at least USD 0.05 per million British thermal units (MMBtu), according to the tender document. items.title: RBI approves SBI MF to acquire up to 9.99% stake in South Indian Bank
items.rss_summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has approved an SBI Mutual Fund's proposal to acquire up to a 9.99 per cent stake in private sector lender South Indian Bank, the bank said in a regulatory filing. The approval was communicated to the bank on November 23 and is subject to compliance with applicable regulatory conditions. "The RBI has accorded its approval to SBI Mutual Fund for acquiring aggregate holding of up to 9.99 per cent of the paid-up share capital or voting rights in the Bank subject to the conditions specified therein," South Indian Bank said in the filing. The approval is subject to compliance with the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, RBI's Directions on Acquisition and Holding of Shares or Voting Rights in Commercial Banks, 2025, the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999, and other applicable laws and regulatory guidelines.
